listening1.context: You are going to hear a conversation between Huda and Salim.

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: Hi Salim! Mr Hilal wants us to hand in our podcast plan on Thursday. Have you got any ideas? I would like to choose a topic that students really care about.

script.speaker: Salim
script.text: Yes, I have. I think we should make a podcast about healthy habits for teenagers. What do you think?

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: That is a good topic, but I am sure many groups will choose it. How about a podcast about school clubs? New students could learn which clubs they might like to join.

script.speaker: Salim
script.text: That is more original. Let's do it! Now, how long should each episode be?

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: I do not think thirty minutes is a good idea. Students lose interest very quickly.

script.speaker: Salim
script.text: I agree. Twenty minutes is still a little long for me. Let's make every episode fifteen minutes.

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: Perfect. Every episode will also need a guest. Who shall we interview in the first episode?

script.speaker: Salim
script.text: I would like to talk to Mr Said, the science club leader. Everybody says he is very funny. Or we could ask Ms Aisha from the drama club.

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: Ms Aisha is travelling this week, so we will invite her for episode two. Mr Said can be our first guest.

script.speaker: Salim
script.text: Great. Now we need a place to record. I have a good microphone at home, but we need a quiet room.

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: The library is too noisy, and the classrooms are busy in the morning. What about the computer lab?

script.speaker: Salim
script.text: Yes, the lab is quiet after school, and it has fast computers for editing. When shall we record?

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: I have English club on Monday. Which day is good for you?

script.speaker: Salim
script.text: I have football practice on Sunday and Tuesday, so Wednesday is the best day for me. Now we need a name for the podcast.

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: I like School Voice. It sounds nice and simple, and it is easy to remember.

script.speaker: Salim
script.text: It is nice, but I prefer Club Corner because it tells listeners what the podcast is about.

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: You are right. Club Corner it is. Finally, where shall we put the episodes? Mr Hilal said we can use the school radio.

script.speaker: Salim
script.text: The radio is a good idea, but I think the school website is better because students can listen at home. Excellent. Let's start writing the first script this afternoon, and we can show it to Mr Hilal tomorrow.

listening2.context: You are going to hear a talk about hydropower.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Good morning, everyone. Today I am going to talk about hydropower, one of the oldest and most important sources of renewable energy.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Hydropower means using the energy of moving water. People discovered this idea a very long time ago. More than two thousand years ago, the ancient Greeks used water wheels to grind grain into flour. The river turned the wheel, and the wheel turned heavy stones. Farmers did not need to use their own strength any more.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Later, engineers learned how to make electricity from water. In eighteen eighty-two, the first hydroelectric power station opened in the United States. After that, many countries began to build dams on their rivers.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: How does a modern hydropower station work? First, a dam holds back a river, and a large lake forms behind it. This lake is called a reservoir. The water in the reservoir has a lot of stored energy. When workers open the gates in the dam, the water rushes down through big pipes. It turns a machine called a turbine, and the turbine turns a generator. The generator then produces electricity.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Today, the biggest hydropower station in the world is the Three Gorges Dam in China. Hydropower gives the world about one sixth of its electricity.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Hydropower has important advantages. It is renewable because rain keeps filling the rivers. It does not burn fuel, so it produces almost no greenhouse gases while it works. It can also provide electricity at any time of the day.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: However, there are some disadvantages. Building a dam is very expensive and takes many years. A dam can also change the life of a river. For example, fish may not be able to swim up the river to lay their eggs. In addition, some people have to leave their homes when a valley is covered by water.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Finally, not every country can use hydropower. A country needs strong rivers and plenty of rain. Oman has only a few rivers that flow all year, and most wadis fill with water only after heavy rain. So Oman uses other sources of energy, such as solar and wind power.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Thank you for listening.

reading1.title: Rainforests: Treasures of the Earth
passage: Rainforests are thick, green forests that grow in warm places where it rains almost every day. A tropical rainforest can receive more than two metres of rain in a year, and the temperature stays warm in every season. Rainforests cover only about six percent of the land on Earth, but they are home to more than half of the world's kinds of plants and animals.

The biggest rainforest is the Amazon in South America. It is shared by several countries, and Brazil has the largest part. The second biggest is the Congo rainforest in Africa. There are also large rainforests in South-East Asia, in countries such as Indonesia and Malaysia.

A rainforest has four main layers. At the top are the tallest trees, called the emergent layer, and some of them grow higher than forty metres. Below them is the canopy, a thick roof of leaves and branches. The canopy is home to most of the animals, such as monkeys, birds and snakes. Under the canopy is the understory, where it is dark and humid. On the ground is the forest floor. Very little sunlight reaches it, so only a few plants can grow there.

Rainforests help our planet in many ways. Trees take in carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas, and give out oxygen. Their roots hold the soil in place, which helps to stop floods in the rainy season. Trees also release water vapour into the air, and this forms clouds. In addition, people use rainforest plants to make medicines, and the forests give us food such as nuts, cocoa and many fruits.

Sadly, rainforests are in danger. People cut down trees for wood, and they clear land to grow crops and to keep cattle. Roads and mines also destroy forest, and fires can spread quickly in dry years. When a forest disappears, animals lose their homes, and some species may become extinct. Fewer trees also mean that more carbon dioxide stays in the air, which adds to global warming.

We can all help to protect rainforests. Governments can make laws that stop illegal cutting. Companies can use wood that comes from well-managed forests. Ordinary people can recycle paper, buy products with a sustainable label and learn more about rainforests. If we act now, these amazing forests will continue to protect the planet for many years.

reading2.title: Ancient Rome
passage: Ancient Rome began as a small town on the River Tiber in Italy. According to legend, it was founded in 753 BC by Romulus, who became its first king. Over the next few centuries, Rome grew from a town into a powerful republic, and then into a great empire.

The Roman Empire began in 27 BC, when Augustus became the first emperor. At its largest, around 117 AD, it stretched from Britain in the north to Egypt in the south, and it included all the lands around the Mediterranean Sea. Millions of people with different languages and cultures lived under Roman rule.

To control such a huge empire, the Romans built thousands of kilometres of straight, strong roads. Soldiers could march quickly along them, and traders could carry goods from one city to another. Many of these roads were so well built that parts of them can still be seen today. People even said, "All roads lead to Rome."

Roman engineers were also famous for their aqueducts. These were long bridges and channels that carried fresh water from the hills into cities. Thanks to aqueducts, Roman cities had public fountains and public baths, where people met friends, relaxed and kept clean. The Romans also used a strong building material called concrete, which allowed them to build huge domes and arches.

Entertainment was important in Roman life. The biggest building for shows was the Colosseum in Rome, which opened in 80 AD. It could hold tens of thousands of people, who came to watch gladiator fights and other events. Chariot races were held in another large stadium called the Circus Maximus.

From the third century AD, the empire faced many problems, including wars, weak emperors and attacks from outside. In 476 AD, the last emperor in the west lost his throne, and the Western Roman Empire came to an end. However, the eastern half continued for nearly one thousand years as the Byzantine Empire.

Rome's ideas have lasted until today. Latin, the language of the Romans, developed into Italian, Spanish, French, Portuguese and Romanian, and many English words also come from Latin. Julius Caesar introduced a new calendar with a year of 365 days and a leap year every four years, and our calendar is based on it. Roman law and the idea of a republic have also influenced many countries.

chart.title: Online Activities of Grade 10 Boys and Girls
chart.model:
The bar chart illustrates the online activities of Grade 10 boys and girls in one school in Oman. Overall, boys preferred playing games, whereas girls preferred using social media.
Firstly, the most popular online activity for boys was playing games, with 70% of students. This was followed by watching videos (60%) and using social media (50%). However, the least popular activity for boys was doing homework, with only 30% of students.
In contrast, the most popular online activity for girls was using social media, with 80% of students. This was followed by watching videos (65%) and doing homework (45%). However, the least popular activity for girls was playing games, with only 20% of students.
To summarize, both boys and girls liked watching videos. However, the biggest difference was in playing games, where 70% of boys chose it, whereas 20% of girls did.

email.situation: Imagine you are Ali. Your school is holding a coding workshop next week.
email.task: Write an email to your friend Khalid and invite him to the workshop. In your email, write about:
bullets: when and where the workshop will be
email.model:
Dear Khalid,

Hello, how are you and your family? I hope you are very well. I am very happy to write to you. I am writing this email to invite you to a coding workshop at my school.

First, the workshop will be held in the computer lab on Thursday at nine o'clock. For example, it will last for three hours. Moreover, a teacher from the university will lead it.

Second, we will learn how to make a simple game. Moreover, it is a great chance to meet new friends. Therefore, please bring your laptop and a notebook.

That's all I have for now. Please write and tell me your news. I am looking forward to hearing from you soon.

Best wishes,
Ali
